blocks.prompt: 12 If \(f(a + x) + f(a - x) = 0\), show that \(\int_{0}^{2a} f(x)\,dx = 0\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh saboot ka sawal hai. Condition ka matlab hai ke \(x = a\) se barabar faasle par \(f\) ki values ulti hain: ek taraf jitni upar, doosri taraf utni neeche.
Diya kya hai? \(f(a + x) + f(a - x) = 0\).
Kya saabit karna hai? \([0, 2a]\) par integral 0 hai; \(a\) is interval ka beech hai.
Rule kaunsa? Property IV: \(x\) ki jagah \(2a - x\). Condition se \(f(2a - x) = -f(x)\) nikal aata hai, to integral apne hi negative ke barabar ho jata hai.
Plan: condition ko nayi shakal, Property IV, equation.
steps:
Diya gaya: har \(x\) ke liye \(f(a + x) + f(a - x) = 0\).
Saabit karna: \(\int_{0}^{2a} f(x)\,dx = 0\).
Tareeqa: Property IV \(\int_0^{2a} f(x)\,dx = \int_0^{2a} f(2a - x)\,dx\).

Condition ko nayi shakal dein
\[x \to a - x:\ f(2a - x) + f(x) = 0\]
\[f(2a - x) = -f(x)\]
Kyun: condition har \(x\) ke liye sach hai, to \(a - x\) ke liye bhi. \(a + (a - x) = 2a - x\) aur \(a - (a - x) = x\). Ab humein woh shakal mil gayi jo Property IV mein chahiye.
Dhyan dein: yeh qadam hi sawal ki chaabi hai; is ke baghair Property IV ka faida nahi uthaya ja sakta.

Property IV lagayein
\[I = \int_{0}^{2a} f(x)\,dx = \int_{0}^{2a} f(2a - x)\,dx\]
\[= -\int_{0}^{2a} f(x)\,dx = -I\]
Kyun: limits ka jama \(0 + 2a\) hai, to \(x\) ki jagah \(2a - x\) rakh sakte hain; phir \(f(2a - x) = -f(x)\) rakha.

Equation hal karein
\[I = -I \Rightarrow 2I = 0 \Rightarrow I = 0\]
Kyun: jo number apne negative ke barabar ho, woh sirf 0 hai.

Tasdeeq: ek misaal se
\[a = 3,\quad f(x) = (x - 3)^3\]
\[\int_{0}^{6} (x - 3)^3\,dx = \left[\dfrac{(x - 3)^4}{4}\right]_{0}^{6}\]
\[= \dfrac{81}{4} - \dfrac{81}{4} = 0 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(f(3 + x) + f(3 - x) = x^3 + (-x)^3 = 0\), condition poori. Integral \(\frac{81}{4} - \frac{81}{4} = 0\) aaya.
